source.authority: National Development Council + Chung-Hua Institution for Economic Research
source.sourceClockRule: For future prospective receipts, use capturedAt unless a native release timestamp finer than publication date is authenticated.

overallManufacturing.interpretation: High aggregate expansion coexists with slowing new-order acceleration and higher delivery/inventory pressure.

keyCounterexample.statement: Longer supplier delivery times are not a monotonic bullish demand signal.
keyCounterexample.evidence: Electronics/optical delivery time reached 73.8 while new-order momentum fell sharply, unfinished-order growth slowed, inventory rose to 64.8 and customer inventory crossed above 50.
keyCounterexample.implication: Delivery-time pressure can represent supply bottlenecks, material mismatch and scheduling friction rather than pure demand acceleration.

backlogSemantics: unfinishedOrders above 50 means expansion of unfinished work/orders, but the level and direction of change must be kept separately.
A high backlog with falling new orders can describe legacy work accumulation rather than fresh demand acceleration.
Supplier delivery-time index must be paired with order, inventory and price states; slower delivery alone is ambiguous.
PMI industry aggregates are industry-level states, not company-specific order books.
Future six-month outlook is survey expectation, not committed backlog.

pitSemantics.firstEligibleDecision: No earlier than release/capture; never backdate to September month-end.
pitSemantics.revisionRule: If NDC/CIER revises a release, append a new vintage and preserve the original captured state.

positiveMechanism: New orders and unfinished orders can separate fresh demand from accumulated work.
Supplier delivery time can expose bottlenecks/lead-time stress when joined with new orders, inventories and prices.
Industry-specific PMI subindices permit Taiwan-native order/lead-time state classification before company-level mapping.
falsification: Long delivery time can coexist with slowing demand; do not assign a fixed positive sign.
Backlog expansion can reflect bottlenecks or inability to deliver, not only strong final demand.
Inventory expansion can be strategic buffering, forced accumulation, or demand mismatch.
PMI survey states are diffusion indices, not physical order quantities.
Industry PMI cannot be directly mapped to an individual listed company's revenue without exposure evidence.
promotionReason: NDC/CIER monthly Taiwan PMI releases expose dated, industry-level new-order, unfinished-order, supplier-delivery, inventory and outlook states with explicit publication dates. The September electronics counterexample demonstrates why these fields must be joined rather than reduced to a single bullish backlog/lead-time number. This establishes Taiwan PIT/source feasibility, not company-level predictive efficacy.
exactNext: SC-040 build an append-only monthly ORDER_LEADTIME_RECEIPT with release/capture clocks and industry state vectors across independent months.
SC-041 map one industry PMI state to listed-company exposure only where product/revenue scope is independently evidenced.
Do not use PMI supplier-delivery time as a direct company score before incremental-value/OOS tests.
